text.p: Mexican industrial holding company Grupo Industrial Saltillo SA de CV (Gissa) said on Thursday that it has acquired the steel business Acero Porcelanizado SA from Mexican glass giant Vitro SA.
The amount of the transaction was not revealed, although representatives of the two companies told Reuters that additional details would be available later Thursday.
Gissa said it would integrate Aceros Porcelanizados into its home products division and that it would be administered by its Cinsa subsidiary.
"Aceros Porcelanizados is one of the most important manufacturing companies for enameled steel for cookware in Mexico," Gissa said in a news release.
"With this deal, Cinsa consolidates itself as the largest maker in the Americas for these kinds of products, and this transaction will increase its sales by 40 percent," the company said.
Operating headquarters for Aceros Porcelanizados will move from Monterrey, Vitro's base, to nearby Saltillo, Gissa's home town.
Gissa also has interests in auto parts, floor coverings, ceramics, bathroom furniture and other household products.
Vitro, one of the world's largest glass makers, has been selling off some of its subsidiaries to concentrate on its core businesses of flat glass, glass containers and white goods.
